blocks.content: While the Finance Commission is a constitutional body tasked with fiscal federalism under Article 280, the Planning Commission was an extra-constitutional body responsible for economic planning.

rows: Five-Year Plan formulation & plan fund allocations

items: Article 280 governs the constitution, powers, and recommendations of the Finance Commission.
Grants-in-aid of revenues to states are recommended under Article 275 by the Finance Commission.
The Planning Commission was established in March 1950 by an executive resolution and replaced by NITI Aayog on January 1, 2015.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution, whereas the Planning Commission was a non-constitutional body created by an executive resolution.
The primary function of the Finance Commission is to determine the devolution of central tax revenues to the states and recommend grants-in-aid under Article 275.
The Planning Commission was tasked with formulating India's Five-Year Plans and allocating plan resources to states and central ministries.
On January 1, 2015, the Planning Commission was dissolved and replaced by NITI Aayog, which operates as a policy think tank without fund allocation powers.
